newsitem.title: USA: Unisys aims for profits in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Unisys aims for profits in 1997.

text.p: Unisys Corp executives said that one of the company's main near term financial goals is to achieve full year profitability, after the payment of preferred dividends, in 1997.
In 1996, Unisys lost $49.7 million, or $0.41 per share, after the payment of preferred dividends.
Company executives said at an analysts' meeting that they also see slight growth in profit margins in 1997, versus total gross margins of 33.3 percent of revenues in 1996.
Unisys Chairman and CEO James Unruh told the meeting that he is "not uncomfortable" with the current range of estimates on Wall Street for the company.

"We are not uncomfortable with the range of estimates that exist out there, but that's all I can tell you," he said in response to one analyst's question about the company's current financial outlook.
According to First Call, the range of estimates on Wall Street for 1997 is for a profit $0.28- $0.50 a share.
Unisys also said that its capital spending in 1997 will decline to $250 million, down from $280 million in 1996.
Unisys executives predicted that its computer systems group will see flat revenues in 1997, compared with revenues of $2.4 billion in 1996.

Although Unisys expects an increase in the number of MIPS shipped (a measure of computing performance) in 1997, revenues will be flat because of increased price performance, meaning it is shipping more powerful computers at a lower cost.
Its computer unit revenue growth will also see an impact from an expected decline in revenues of its ClearPath system, which will offset the growth in personal computer revenues.
Unisys also said that it expects its Information Services Group to achieve operating profitability in the second half.
The company is further reducing its sales, general and administrative expenses in this business unit, because expenses were at unacceptable levels in 1996.
